teams.heading: Frank Lomani laments second-half errors as Japan snatch Fiji's PNC title
teams.body: The Flying Fijians failed to defend their Pacific Nations Cup title on Saturday, falling 20-15 to Japan in a tense final in Tokyo. Despite leading 12-10 at the interval following tries from Virimi Vakatawa and captain Tevita Ikanivere, Fiji succumbed to a late Samisoni Tua score. Halfback Frank Lomani admitted the squad were "gutted" after mistakes and poor discipline — including a Mesake Doge yellow card — allowed the hosts to dominate possession and territory during the closing stages.

lead.why: The loss in the Pacific Nations Cup final is the most significant news regarding the senior men's team today.

teams.heading: England women share spoils as Canada draw halts record-breaking winning run
teams.body: The Red Roses saw their remarkable 39-match winning streak come to a conclusion at Sandy Park, as Canada held the world champions to a 26-26 draw. Despite the result, John Mitchell’s side remains unbeaten in 40 Tests. England led through tries from Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, Hannah Botterman, and Bryony Field but were unable to convert sustained pressure into a victory during a chaotic final quarter. Mitchell remains optimistic, stating, "I'm a realist; there will be greater things come as a result of this."

lead.why: The end of a historic 39-match winning streak for the Red Roses is the most significant development in the sport this morning.

teams.heading: France women overcome 19-point deficit to defeat Australia in Aix-en-Provence
teams.body: The France women’s side conjured a remarkable 29-26 comeback win against Australia on Saturday, despite being reduced to 11 players during a chaotic first half at the Stade Maurice David. The match was further disrupted when a bus caught fire adjacent to the stadium, delaying the second-half restart. Despite suffering a sixth card after the break, France reeled off 17 unanswered points in the final 25 minutes to turn a 26-12 deficit into a victory, frustrating the Wallaroos.

teams.heading: Ireland women surrender 19-point lead in narrow defeat to USA
teams.body: Ireland women suffered a frustrating 40-36 defeat against the USA in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium on Saturday. Scott Bemand’s side dominated the opening period, leading 31-12 early in the second half, before a loss of discipline and a yellow card for Vicky Elmes Kinlan allowed the visitors to rally with four successive tries. Bemand admitted the result was "a game we should have won," as his side now looks to respond in upcoming fixtures against Japan.

teams.heading: Italy women dominate Japan 55-21 in WXV Global Series tournament opener
teams.body: The Italy women's side opened their WXV Global Series campaign with a commanding 55-21 victory over the Sakura XV at Stadio Omero Tognon. After briefly trailing early, the Azzurre responded with a flurry of tries from Alyssa D'Inca, Vittoria Vecchini, and Giordana Duca to seize control. Captain Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi marked her 50th cap with a second-half score, helping Italy record their highest-ever points tally against Japan in a dominant display that saw the visitors outplayed in all facets.

teams.heading: Scotland women suffer heavy 66-14 defeat against dominant New Zealand side
teams.body: The Scotland women's team conceded 10 tries in a challenging 66-14 defeat to New Zealand at Hive Stadium. Despite the scoreline, Evie Gallagher provided some attacking spark for the hosts, crossing for two first-half tries to keep Scotland in contention at 24-14. However, the world number two side controlled the remainder of the match with relentless pace and clinical finishing. Scotland will look to regroup before facing Australia at the same venue in their next WXV fixture.

teams.heading: Wales women deliver statement performance in eight-try demolition of South Africa
teams.body: The Wales women's side secured an emphatic 50-19 victory over South Africa in their WXV Global Series opener at Cardiff Arms Park. Head coach Sean Lynn praised his squad's new DNA, noting the significant growth in skill development that underpinned their dominant eight-try performance. Co-captain Alex Callender earned player of the match honours, while Sisilia Tuipulotu impressed with a brace of tries. “This is just the start for us, this is going to be our new DNA,” Lynn said following the result.

teams.heading: UAR continues search for permanent head coach as vacancy remains open
teams.body: The search for a permanent head coach for Los Pumas remains unresolved as the Argentine Rugby Union continues its evaluation process. While recent media reports have linked Jacques Nienaber to the position, there has been no confirmation of an appointment or formal agreement. The role remains vacant following previous cycles, and the union has yet to provide an official update regarding their preferred candidate or a timeline for when an announcement might be expected.

teams.heading: Jordan Petaia returns to Wallabies squad for upcoming Springboks Test
teams.body: Jordan Petaia has been recalled to the Wallabies squad following his brief stint with the NFL’s Los Angeles Chargers. The 26-year-old, who last represented Australia at the 2023 World Cup, revealed he was misdiagnosed while attempting to play through a hamstring tendon injury during his American football transition. Coach Les Kiss has included the utility back in his 34-man squad for the upcoming Test against South Africa, as Australia look to build on a five-match unbeaten run.

teams.heading: Japan edge past Fiji to secure Pacific Nations Cup tournament victory
teams.body: Japan claimed their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019, defeating holders Fiji 20-15 in a physical encounter at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium on Saturday. After trailing at half-time, the Brave Blossoms rallied through a second-half try from flanker Ben Gunter and a decisive late score from Samisoni Tua. Captain Naoto Saito, who was named player of the tournament, noted, "It’s a great breakthrough to create history for Japan. It gives this young team great confidence."

teams.heading: Ardie Savea faces lengthy layoff following required surgery on dislocated shoulder
teams.body: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea is set for a significant period on the sidelines after New Zealand Rugby confirmed he requires surgery on a dislocated shoulder. The injury was sustained during the third Test against the Springboks in Soweto. With rehabilitation typically taking around six months, his availability for the upcoming Nations Championship remains in doubt. Savea’s absence compounds a mounting injury list, which includes fellow loose forward Luke Jacobson and winger Caleb Clarke, both of whom face several months of recovery.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus releases Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende early
teams.body: Coach Rassie Erasmus has sent two key Springboks home early to be with their families following a heavy workload during the recent series against the All Blacks. Flank Pieter-Steph du Toit and centre Damian de Allende will miss this week's one-off Test against the Wallabies in Perth. Erasmus confirmed that he is comfortable with the depth available in his travelling squad to cover these absences, prioritising player welfare after the intense international schedule.
